 JUDGMENT
The petitioners have filed this claim petition against respondents seeking compensation on account of death of the deceased Sri.Akhileshvara.M S/o Mani.S, who died in Motor Vehicle Accident.

02. The brief facts of the case of the petitioners is as under:
On 14.01.2023 at about 09.45 p.m, the deceased Akhileshvara.M being a rider of Motor Cycle bearing No.KA-02-HP-7392 was going on NH-4, Tumkur- Bangalore Main Road, Nelamangala towards 8th Mile, (SCCH-3) 3 M.V.C.No.1083/2023 in front of Savani Transport Office, very carefully and cautiously at minimum speed, at that time, one Lorry bearing No.KA-10-6383 was negligently parked on the middle of the main road by its driver, in a negligent manner, without any signal or indicator or even without putting any barricade and even without putting any man to signal at a very busy road that too on the dark night time, the deceased Akhileshvara.M unaware of that negligently parked lorry and when he realized that that lorry was parked on the middle of the road, he had almost reached near the said lorry and to avoid the collusion he tried his best and applied the brake.
But by that time his Motor Cycle has dashed against back side of the said lorry.
Due to impact, the said Akhileshvara.M fell down and sustained grievous injuries and succumbed to injuries at the spot.
The petitioners have spent Rs.50,000/- towards transportation of deadbody and funeral expenses.

Prior to accident the deceased was hale and healthy and was aged about 25 years and was working as Executive, Grade-II at Matrix Business Services India Private Limited and drawing salary of Rs.25,000/- p.m and he was the sole earner of the family.

entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: The petitioner No.1 father and petitioner No.2 younger sister of the deceased.

The accident was occurred due to negligent (SCCH-3) 4 M.V.C.No.1083/2023 parking of the above said offending lorry on the middle of the road by its driver and in this regard the Peenya Traffic Police have registered a case against driver of said lorry.
The respondent No.1 being the insurer and respondent No.2 being the owner of the offending lorry
, are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation of Rs.50,00,000/- with interest and costs.
03. On service of notice, the respondents No.1 and 2 have appeared before the tribunal through their respective counsels, but only the respondent No.1 has filed written statement.

04. The respondent No.1 in its written statement has denied the entire case of the petitioners and further denied the alleged negligent parking of lorry by the driver of the lorry, causing accident,
death of deceased and also denied age, occupation, income of deceased and dependency of the petitioners and expenses incurred by the petitioners and admits that the Lorry bearing Mani.S vs Hdfc Ergo General Ins Co Ltd on 11 March, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/4803931/
2 No.KA-10-6383 was duly insured with this respondent and the same is valid as on the date of accident and the liability is subject to terms and conditions of the policy.

Further contended that the offending lorry was not at all involved in the alleged accident and the deceased was riding two-wheeler in a rash and negligent manner and dashed to their vehicle (SCCH-3) 5 M.V.C.No.1083/2023 which was parked in proper line of the road and the driver of their insured vehicle not having a valid and effective driving licence and not having permit at the time of accident.
The compensation claimed is exaggerated.
Hence, pray for dismiss the petition against respondent No.1 with costs.

05. On the basis of the above pleadings of the parties, this tribunal has framed the following Issues:-
ISSUES 01.
Whether petitioners prove that they are the LRs/dependents of deceased Sri.Akhileshwara.M S/o Mani?

02. Whether petitioners prove that deceased Sri.Akhileshwara.M S/o Mani was died in RTA arising out of the accident alleged to have been taken place on 14.01.2023 at about 9.45 p.m, opposite Savani Transport, NH-4 Tumakuru Road, near Toll,
Bengaluru, due to negligent parking of Lorry bearing registration No.KA-10-6383 by its driver as alleged in the petition?
03. Whether petitioners are entitled for compensation?
If so, what amount & from whom?
04 . What order or award?
06. The petitioners in order to prove their case, petitioner No.1 is examined himself as PW.1 and got marked 16 documents as Ex.P.1 to 16 and closed their (SCCH-3) 6 M.V.C.No.1083/2023 side evidence.
On the otherhand, the Legal Manager of the respondent No.1 Insurance Company examined as RW.1 and got marked 1 document as Ex.R.1 and closed its side evidence.
07. The counsels for the petitioners and respondent No.1 argued on the main matter and perused the records.

08. My findings on the above Issues are as follows:
 Issue No.1 : In the Affirmative  Issue No.2 : In the Affirmative  Issue No.3 : Partly in the Affirmative  Issue No.4 : As per final order  for the following:-

sentences.text: 09 . Issues No.1 and 2:-

Since these two issues are interconnected to each other and in order to avoid repetition of facts and appreciation of evidence on record, these two issues are taken together for common consideration and discussion.
10. The petitioners in order to prove their case, the petitioner No.1 is examined as PW.1 and in his chief-examination evidence he has reiterated the (SCCH-3) 7 M.V.C.No.1083/2023 petition averments.

Though he has been elaborately cross-examined by the respondent No.1 counsel, but nothing has been brought on record to disbelieve the case of the petitioners and during cross-examination he denied to the suggestion

that his son while returning to his home, hurridly,
negligently and rashly riding his Motor Cycle and dashed against the lorry.
11.
Apart from the oral evidence, the petitioners have got marked 16 documents as Ex.P.1 to 16 on their behalf.
Ex. P.1 is copy of FIR filed by the Peenya Traffic Police against driver/respondent No.2 of offending Lorry for negligent parking the lorry on the main road, caused accident and death of deceased.
Ex.P.2 is copy of Complaint.
Ex.P.3 is copy of Spot Mahazar with Sketch.
Ex.P.4 is copy of Photograph of Lorry.
Ex.P.5 is copy of Inquest panchanama of deceased Akhileshvara.
M. Ex.P.6 is copy of Post mortem report of deceased Akhileshvara.M wherein it is stated that cause of death is due to head injury sustained.
Ex.P.7 is copy of Notice U/Sec.133 of IMV Act issued to the owner of the offending lorry.

Ex.P.8 is copy of Reply to notice which discloses that the owner- cum-driver of the offending lorry has stated that he was driving the lorry as on the date of accident and he had a valid driving licence and said offending lorry had (SCCH-3) 8 M.V.C.No.1083/2023 valid insurance with respondent No.1 and the same is valid as on the date of accident.
Ex.P.9 is copy of IMV report which discloses that both vehicles are involved in the accident and both vehicles are damaged.

Ex.P.10 is copy of Charge sheet which discloses that the Investigation Officer after thorough investigation has submitted Charge sheet against driver/respondent No.2 of the offending lorry for negligent parking of the lorry and causing accident and causing death of deceased.
Ex.P.13 is copy of Driving licence of deceased.

Ex.P.14 is copy of Aadhaar card of petitioner No.1, Ex.P.15 is copy of Aadhaar card of petitioner No.2 and Ex.P.16 is copy of Aadhaar card of deceased Akhileshvara.M.
12.

On going through the entire oral and documentary evidence produced by the petitioners, it is clearly establishes that petitioner No.1 is the father and petitioner No.2 is the sister of deceased and they are legal representatives and dependents on the income of the deceased.

It is also proved and established that the deceased Akhileshvara.M was died in road traffic accident that occurred on 14.01.2023 at about 09.45 p.m, on NH-4, Tumkur-Bangalore Main Road, Nelamangala towards 8th Mile, in front of Savani Transport Office, due to negligent parking of Lorry (SCCH-3) 9 M.V.C.No.1083/2023 bearing No.KA-10-6383 by its driver.
Accordingly, Issues No.1 and 2 are answered in the affirmative.
13. Issue No.3:- This issue is related to the entitlement of the compensation on account of the death of the deceased Akhileshvara.M, who died in the Motor Vehicle Accident.

The PW.1/petitioner No.1 has stated that prior to accident deceased was hale and healthy and was Mani.S vs Hdfc Ergo General Ins Co Ltd on 11 March, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/4803931/
4 aged about 25 years and was working as Executive, Grade-II at Matrix Business Services India Private Limited and drawing salary of Rs.25,000/- p.m and he was the sole earner of the family and they have spent Rs.50,000/- towards transportation of deadbody and funeral expenses.

14. It is the duty of the petitioners to prove age, avocation and income of the deceased as on the date of accident.
The petitioners have not produced any birth certificate, school records or SSLC marks card of the deceased to show the exact date of birth of the deceased.
However, they have produced Ex.P.13 Driving licence and Ex.P.16 Aadhaar card of deceased.

Eventhough the said documents are not authenticated document for the proof of age of any person, but in the (SCCH-3) 10 M.V.C.No.1083/2023 absence of other evidence, these documents can be relied upon and according to which his date of birth is mentioned as 25.11.1996.
The alleged accident occurred on 14.01.2023.
Hence, it appears that as on the date of accident the deceased is aged 26 years.
Therefore, this tribunal has assessed the age of the deceased as 26 years as on the date of accident.

As per the ratio laid down by the Apex Court in a decision reported in 2009 ACJ 1298 in between Sarla Verma and Ors. V/s. Delhi Transport Corporation and Ors. case the multiplier applicable to the age group of 26 to 30 years is 17.
15.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: So far as avocation and income of deceased is concerned, the petitioners have produced Ex.P.11 Letter of appointment dt:16.06.2021 and Ex.P.12 Pay slip for the month of November 2022 issued by one Matrix Business Services India Private Limited.

entities.text: Matrix Business Services India Private Limited
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: But the petitioners have not examined the employer of said company and even they have not examined the author of Ex.P.11 and 12.

Therefore,
said documents cannot be relied upon without examining the author or employer of said documents.

Therefore, in the absence of satisfactory evidence regarding avocation and income of the deceased,
this tribunal has relied upon notional income as per the chart issued by Karnataka (SCCH-3) 11 M.V.C.No.1083/2023 State Legal Services Authority, Bengaluru and as per norms for the year 2023 the notional income is Rs.16,000/- p.m and hence, this tribunal has assessed the income of the deceased at Rs.16,000/- p.m and it is multiplied by 12.
16.
In the case on hand, petitioner No.1 is the father and petitioner No.2 is the unmarried sister of deceased and they are dependents on the income of the deceased.

In view of the ratio laid down by the Hon'ble Apex Court in a decision reported in (2017) 16 SCC 680 in between National Insurance Co. Ltd., V/s Pranay Sethi & Others case, the future prospects or additional income should be added to monthly income of the deceased.

entities.text: National Insurance Co. Ltd., V/s Pranay Sethi & Others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Since deceased was aged about 26 years at the time of accident and was self employee, 40% income should be added to the monthly income towards future prospects which would be result in the income to be (16,000 + 6,400) = Rs.22,400/-.

It is also evident that deceased was a bachelor, it is appropriate to deduct 50% of the income of the deceased towards personal and living expenses of the deceased and then his monthly income would be (22,400 - 11,200) = Rs.11,200/-.
The income of the deceased for the purpose of determining the loss of dependency would thus be Rs.11,200/-.
As the (SCCH-3) 12 M.V.C.No.1083/2023 deceased was aged about 26 years, the multiplier of 17 would have to be applied.
Consequently the claimants would be entitled for a sum of Rs.22,84,800/- (Rs.11,200 x 12 x 17) towards loss of dependency.

18. The claimant No.1 is the father and claimant No.2 is the unmarried sister of the deceased.

In view of the ratio laid down by the Hon'ble Apex Court in a decision reported in Magma General Insurance Company Ltd., V/s Nanu Ram alias Churu Ram reported in (2018) 18 SCC 130, the petitioner No.1 is entitled for Rs.40,000/- towards loss of filial consortium and the petitioner No.2 is entitled for Rs.40,000/- towards loss of love and affection and petitioners are entitled for Rs.19,500/- each towards loss of estate and funeral expenses and transportation of dead body.

Considering the facts and circumstances of the case and noticing the (SCCH-3) 13 M.V.C.No.1083/2023 number of dependents and 50% of the income taken into consideration towards the personal and living expenses of the deceased, this Tribunal has placed reliance on ratio laid down by the Hon'ble Apex Court in a decision reported in (2017) 16 SCC 680 in between National Insurance Co. Ltd., V/s. Pranay Sethi & others case has calculated compensation as under;
 Sl. Head of Amount in  No. Compensation Rs.
 1. Loss of Dependency 22,84,800-00  (After deducting 50% of  the income towards  personal and living  expenses)
 2. Loss of filial consortium 40,000-00  (petitioner No.1)
 3. Loss of love and affection 40,000-00  (petitioner No.2)
 4. Loss of estate 19,500-00

sentences.text: 5 . Funeral expenses and 19,500-00  transportation of dead  body  Total 24,03,800-00 19.

Accordingly I hold that, the petitioners are entitled for total compensation of Rs.24,03,800/-
with (SCCH-3) 14 M.V.C.No.1083/2023 interest at the rate of 6% p.a. from the date of petition till its realization.
20.

Regarding liability:- The respondent No.1 Insurance Company in order to prove its defence and to disprove the case of the petitioners, its Legal Manager is examined as RW.1 and in her chief-examination evidence she has reiterated the written statement averments therein.

During the course of cross-examination by the petitioners counsel she admits that she has no personal knowledge about the accident and they have conducted enquiry regarding the accident but she has not produced any enquiry report before the tribunal and that on behalf of the respondent No.1 Insurance Company, copy of Policy is marked as Ex.R.1, which shows that the respondent No.1 has Mani.S vs Hdfc Ergo General Ins Co Ltd on 11 March, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/4803931/
6 issued insurance policy in favour of respondent No.2 and the same is valid from 31.03.2022 to 30.03.2023 and the alleged accident was occurred on 14.01.2023.

sentences.text: Therefore, it appears that as on the date of accident the insurance policy of the offending vehicle is valid and is in force.
The respondent No.1 has not placed any material to show that the owner or driver of the offending vehicle have violated the terms and conditions of the policy.

Therefore, the respondent No.1 being the insurer and (SCCH-3) 15 M.V.C.No.1083/2023 respondent No.2 being the owner of the offending Lorry, are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioners.

However,
since policy of offending vehicle was valid and is in force as on the date of accident, respondent No.1 being the insurer of offending vehicle shall pay above said compensation amount of Rs.24,03,800/-
with interest at the rate of 6% p.a to the petitioners from the date of filing of the petition till the date of deposit.
Accordingly, this Issue is answered partly in the affirmative.
21. Issue No.4:

In view of the above reasoning and discussions to the above Issues No.1 to 3, I proceed to pass the following:-
ORDER
The petition filed by the petitioners under Sec.166 of the M.V. Act, 1989 is partly allowed with costs.

The petitioners are entitled for compensation of Rs.24,03,800/- (Rupees Twenty four lakhs three thousand and eight hundred only) with interest at the rate of 6% p.a from the date of petition till its realization.
(SCCH-3) 16 M.V.C.No.1083/2023 The respondent No.1 shall deposit above said compensation amount with interest within two months from the date of this Judgment.
The petitioner No.1 being the father and petitioner No.2 being sister of the deceased were apportioned the compensation in the ratio of 50-50, in the award amount together with interest.

The petitioners No.1 and 2 are entitled to get release 70% each of the award amount through E-payment directly to their account by obtaining the bank account details and remaining 30% each shall be kept in Fixed Deposit in any Scheduled Bank for a period of three years, in their respective names.
The Advocate fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/-.
Draw award accordingly.

The petition filed by the petitioners under Sec.166 of the M.V. Act, 1989 is partly allowed with costs.
The petitioners are entitled for compensation of Rs.24,03,800/- (Rupees Twenty four lakhs three thousand and eight hundred only) with interest at the rate of 6% p.a from the date of petition till its realization.
(SCCH-3) 16 M.V.C.No.1083/2023 The respondent No.1 shall deposit above said compensation amount with interest within two months from the date of this Judgment.
The petitioner No.1 being the father and petitioner No.2 being sister of the deceased were apportioned the compensation in the ratio of 50-50, in the award amount together with interest.
The petitioners No.1 and 2 are entitled to get release 70% each of the award amount through E-payment directly to their account by obtaining the bank account details and remaining 30% each shall be kept in Fixed Deposit in any Scheduled Bank for a period of three years, in their respective names.
The Advocate fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/-.
Draw award accordingly.
